blocks.text: Lucy Letby - Examination-in-chief day 5: Babies N, O, P & Q
Cross-examination - day 1: General topics
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON
Housekeeping
Wednesday, 17 May 2023
(In the absence of the jury)
As I said I would, Mr Johnson, I've prepared a list of non-sitting days as of today. I hope you have a copy.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We do, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I believe it to be correct. I'll have that distributed to the jury. I don't know whether -- yes, I see Ms Moritz saying they've got one as well.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS (continued)

Ms Letby, yesterday afternoon we concluded looking at the second event relating to [Baby N], which is count 18, and so we're looking at the third event now, which is count 19 on our indictment, and that is the event on the afternoon of 15 June, shortly after 3 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So to help all of us with this and to help you with the facts, let's put up your note that dealt with this, which is at tile 233 of the second [Baby N] sequence. Let's have a look at that and just read in what it was that you said.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: If we go into the note, please. We're going across to the lower left-hand side, Mr Murphy, if we could enlarge that, please.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Can you see there's a note there, Ms Letby, for 15 June. The note is it made at 18.30. Can you see that?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We know this has followed events in the morning when there had been the attempts to intubate after the desaturation at 7.15. Can you read for us, please, what the note says? I'll tell you what to stop or if there's anything I need to ask you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Infant has had periods of apnoea during the morning requiring stimulation and increased oxygen/PEEP. Improving by afternoon. Observations stable. Remains cool so incubator temperature increased. Approx 14.50, infant became apnoeic with desaturation to 44%, heart rate 90. Fresh blood noted from mouth and 3ml blood aspirated from NG tube. Neopuff commenced and doctors crash called. Events documented in medical notes."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's read on a little bit further, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Unable to obtain secure airway. Regs [Dr D] and Mayberry, Consultants Brearey and Saladi unable to insert ET tube. Assistance gained from anaesthetic team. X2 consultants also unable to secure ET tube. Intubation drugs given as prescribed. I-Gel airway inserted and infant ventilated via this. Secured with ties from vent hat."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We'll stop there. Taking a couple of the details there, that last detail: I-Gel airway inserted and infant ventilated..."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Do you remember yesterday we looked on the chart where you'd written "intubation "round about -- the timing varied across the two charts, but we have seen where you wrote "intubation"?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that what you were referring to?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Earlier in the note where there's a reference to 3ml of blood, can we move across to the left-hand side and the lower part, please, Mr Murphy?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Where we can see right in the body of that, the centre of it:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Fresh blood noted from mouth and 3ml blood aspirated from NG tube."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Do you remember we saw where that's recorded on the chart with the initials [Initials of Nurse B] next to it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's the reference to the --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- 3ml, is it? Do you recall what part [Nurse B] played in these events as they were going along?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Not from my memory now, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you have a recollection, a clear recollection, of how events unfolded -- we can take the note down for the time being -- after this event at 14.50?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: After this event here?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I have some memory, not in any great detail.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What was the atmosphere like concerning [Baby N] as that afternoon went on? We see there were these multiple attempts at intubation.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was becoming increasingly chaotic. More and more staff were coming to try and assist. There was a sense of panic around the unit, I think, that we weren't sure how we were going to manage [Baby N].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember how many people were present as the afternoon went on, how many people gathered?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There were loads of people, I would say 10 to 15.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you his designated nurse during this?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you the only person caring for him at any point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, [Baby N] needed such care that he always had at least two members of staff with him. I remember [Nurse B] helping a lot and the doctors were near enough in the room the whole time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you recall what the plans were as the afternoon went into the afternoon and there were continuing concerns about intubating [Baby N]? And I mean intubating with an ETT.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, once the Countess of Chester anaesthetic team had come over and not been able to intubate, a discussion took place
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: with Alder Hey and it was decided that a team from Alder Hey would come out to assess [Baby N].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you have all the drugs you need to treat him given his condition? I'm talking --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We didn't have factor VIII.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You didn't have factor VIII. If we just go back to the note we had up on the screen, tile 233, and go across to the right-hand side and the lower part of the entry we finished with. If we scroll down a little further, this is the entry timed 18.30. What's the final comment at 18.30 that you put in?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Factor VIII brought to unit by specialist nurse at Alder Hey Children's Hospital."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. So what was going on that led to you putting that comment on the note?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Once [Baby N] -- he had blood back from his tube throughout the day and the medical team felt that he needed -we needed to have factor VIII and there was none on the unit for him.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We know a dose had been given round about 11 o'clock that morning.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that was mum's.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That was the mum's?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was mum's factor VIII, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How long had [Baby N] been on the unit for by this point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Since his birth.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Since 2 June?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And he was known to be somebody who had a low factor VIII requirement?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And there was none available for him on the unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, and then it became a panic and therefore it was couriered over then from Alder Hey.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that what that refers to --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- where it says:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Factor VIII brought to unit by specialist nurse at Alder Hey"?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, as an emergency.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can you describe events for us as we move then towards the point when we know the Alder Hey team arrived, going into the evening now?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Before the team arrived?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. We can take the note down for the time being, although we will be going back again.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There was continual intervention with [Baby N] throughout that time. I believe baptism was offered at some point to the parents. There was just lots going on in the room.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember when the Alder Hey team did arrive?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's Dr Potter and the doctors who were with him, is that correct --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- Dr Francis Potter? Can you describe to us what happened? We know there's a further desaturation soon after that. Can you describe to us those events, Ms Letby?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The team from Alder Hey came and there was a lot of discussion and handover going on around the nursery area as to what we were going to do for [Baby N] and the Alder Hey team had brought specialist equipment with them and also wanted to set up a theatre in the labour suite in case we needed to advance to a surgical airway, so there was a lot of discussion and planning going on around that. At this time handover was taking place as well, so the night staff had arrived.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What time are you talking about roughly?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Around 7.30 in the evening. And during that time that's when the episode happened.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, lets just try and get some specific times just to help with that. I'm going to ask Mr Murphy to put up the clinical note made by[Dr D], the doctor who dealt with some of these events in the afternoon, and it's tile 420, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So this is a note [Dr D] made at 21.05 that evening, I am not going to read out all of it, we spent so me time looking at in evidence, but we can see the list of doctors who participated in events to intubate [Baby N] there. Do you see those, Ms Letby?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we scroll down a little further, let's look at the timings. Thank you. We've got Dr Potter, Dr Lakin, ENT consultant arrived around 19.15 for assistance; is that the timing roughly as you recall that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you describe the event took place. It says here:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "19.40, desaturation. 80 down to 50 down to 40s and associated bradycardia."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, does that fit with your recollection of timings approximately?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it does, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We also note here it says here to the right:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Intubated first attempt, size 3 centimetre ETT at 19.53 by Dr Potter."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you recall [Baby N] being intubated?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's just see, for conclusion, your note regarding this which is at tile 233. It's on the right-hand side of the central entry. Can you assist us with what you've put into the system at 20.53 that day?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Medical team from Alder Hey Children's Hospital, ENT and anaesthetics, arrived approximately 19.00. Assessed [Baby N] and decision made to attempt intubation in CLS theatre and advance to tracheostomy if required. Equipment and medications sourced. Observations stable. At 19.40 profound desaturation to 30s with colour loss. Stiff and back arching, became bradycardic. Neopuff
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: in 100% oxygen commenced via I-Gel airway. Mottled ++. Doctors present. Resuscitation commenced as documented. Drugs and fluids checked by myself and Staff Nurse Simcock. Care handed over. All events took place on NNU prior to moving to CLS theatres. Transport team arrived 20.40. Medical care led by intensivist from Alder Hey and Consultant Gibbs."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Thank you for that. Do you recall who was present at the time that this desaturation happened at 19.40?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There were multiple staff there.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can you help us with specifically who or not? I'm not asking that critically just asking if you can --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I know I was talking to Belinda Simcock at that time, handing over. I couldn't recall exactly who was where but there were multiple members of staff.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How much of a focus was [Baby N] for all the medical staff present?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: He was the focus of the whole unit at that point.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Thank you. How were you feeling as events were building up round about 7 o'clock through to the point that [Baby N] was intubated?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: He was a real concern, we were all very worried about him. And to have that many experienced staff intubating and not be able to secure a tube, we were really concerned for [Baby N].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And we had evidence from [Dr D] about you appearing to be stressed or anxious at the time that the team turned up from Alder Hey. Is that a fair description?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I was.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And why were you stressed and anxious by that point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was something I'd never experienced before and I have never known staff to come from other hospitals or other departments within the hospital. I had never seen that many people in the nursery for one baby.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What was the concern at that point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The concern was that if we couldn't get an airway for [Baby N] he would have to undergo surgery, which again is something I'd never seen or heard of before.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How did that make you feel, the thought of [Baby N] undergoing surgery like that in those circumstances?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was frightening.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: For what, or who?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: For his safety. We wanted him to be well and the fact that we couldn't manage his airway was concerning.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Who did take handover over this period?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Belinda Simcock.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We know that [Baby N] was intubated --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- and in due course stabilised. I'm going to move -again, it seems abrupt, dealing with it like this, not intended, but I'm going to move next to count 20, a count relating to [Baby O] or [Baby O] as he's also called.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We've got [Baby O] and [Baby P] on counts 20 and 21, but we'll look at what happened with [Baby O] first and then look at matters relating to [Baby P]. I'm going to ask if we could start then with the first -- well, tile 2 of [Baby O], please. Can we have a look at what's behind that, please?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So [Baby O]. Born 21 June 2016 at 14.24 hours.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Triplet, second of triplets. 33 weeks and 2 days' gestation. 2,020 grams, so a little over 2 kilograms in weight. Born by caesarean.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just to remind you, Ms Letby, and the ladies and gentlemen of the jury, we've got a sequence of babies we look at in this period, as you probably recall.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Count 20 deals with [Baby O] and events on 23 June 2016. Count 21 deals with [Baby P] and events on 24 June and then you may recall, ladies and gentlemen, count 22 is concerned with [Baby Q] and events on 25 June. So there's a sequence that we're dealing with there.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we just keep that in mind because one matter runs into another to some extent. We'll look at the detail again, as we have been doing when we come to your evidence, Ms Letby, but can I just help us all by reminding you and the jury what count 20 is in its most basic elements.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It relates to the 23rd. There are three particular timings that we looked at, though of course there's various events as we go along. So on 23 June, at 13.15, so just after 1 o'clock in the afternoon, there was vomiting and abdominal distension that [Baby O] experienced.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Then at 14.40, he underwent a profound desaturation and bradycardia and was noted to be mottled and his abdomen red. And then at 15.51, he desaturated to the 30s with bradycardia and required CPR. And sadly, died at 17.47.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we have a sequence of timings there: 13.15, 14.40 and 15.51. Again, I emphasise, there's other details in the evidence; I'm just trying to assist by picking out the key timings.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You'll recall, Ms Letby, as the jury will, that on post-mortem, amongst other findings in the case of [Baby O], there was identified a subcapsular haematoma or haematomas on the liver and we saw images of that, smaller ones in the case of [Baby P], more marked in the case of [Baby O], again to help us with our recollection.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: In the case of [Baby N], we've had events that took us up to 15 June. Do you recall what was happening in your life between the end of those shifts on 15 June and when we come to this sequence of dates on 23 June?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I'd been away on holiday with [Nurse E] and another friend.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Let's have a look at the shift pattern if we could, which is at -- the relevant one we're looking at here now, thank you, Mr Murphy, is at page 33229. If we just enlarge the upper part of that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Do you remember we'd looked yesterday at the messages that refer to doing six long days in the course of 8 days?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That was the 8th through to 15 June; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And 15 June was where we started this morning with [Baby N]. So what was happening over the 16th through to 22nd when we look at the grey patch on this?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So I was abroad on holiday.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The 23rd, is that the first day back?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Thank you. Can we put up the message, please, at tile 21, Mr Murphy? We'll look at a number of messages.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We've got a series of messages that we have exchanged before you start on the shift, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 21, a message at 14.10 of the 22nd. So is this the day you got back off holiday?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that the actual day you arrived back in the UK?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And it's from Jennifer Jones-Key to you, it says:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "The triplets have delivered. [Nurse D] texted as me to work tonight or Friday. When you back in? [as read]"
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Can we go to the next tile, please?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You reply:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Yeah, I heard. Days tomorrow, Fri, Sat."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So when was it you knew that you'd be working on those days, Ms Letby? Or do you know when it was you knew you'd be working those days?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. Move on, please, to tile 23.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Jennifer Jones-Key saying to you after that:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Aw, hope you get some rest today."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 24, your reply to Jennifer Jones-Key:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Yep, probably be back in with a bang lol."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we understand what you mean by that, what do you mean by "back in with a bang lol"?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That I'd come back to work and be straight into a busy shift.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Does it indicate you were planning something dramatic and terrible when you got back?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Tile 25, please. Jennifer Jones-Key to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Probably lol. You'll be fine though, you don't mind being busy. I'm annoyed they're trying to get us in when trying to get rid of us, so I've said no."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And the next tile, please, your response to Jennifer Jones-Key:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "I do, lol. Yeah, can completely understand that plus unfair to keep asking when you're on annual leave."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: When you're saying, "I do lol", what are you saying you agree with?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Sorry, can I just see the one before?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, can we put up tile 25, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Oh, "Enjoy being busy". Yes, she said I cope okay with being busy.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When you were asked to work shifts, how ready were you to go in and do extra shifts?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I was very available.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why was that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Because I had no other commitments outside work and I lived very close to the hospital. I was very amenable to changing and helping the unit when I could.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Thank you. Can we go next, please, to tile 39. Still the same day but a little later on. We'll look at several tiles here. This is a message from [Dr A] to you, 17.13 that day:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "How was the flight? Unpacked as well. It's the only way. Washing machine on? Day has been rubbish [emoji]. Lots of unnecessary stress for NNU and too much work to fit into one day [emoji]. I may have overfilled the unit again. SHOs have all been fed and watered and the babies are generally okay so maybe not as bad as I'm thinking."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Your response at tile 40:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Glad it's over but flight was and airport was fine, thanks. On second load of washing. Oh, that's not good. Back to earth with a bump for me tomorrow then. You seem to be quite good at acquiring babies to fill our empty cots. Good work, reg, but I'm guessing you've not been fed and watered."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And the response to that, please, from [Dr A] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "It's a skill I've had for years. To be fair, there wasn't a social admission. Yes, you might be a bit busy. Oh, you're right: I made sure they went first. just realised when I last ate. Oops."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, was there anything unusual about being busy like this on the unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When Jennifer Jones-Key in the text earlier, the messages, has said to you something about trying to get -- "I'm annoyed they're trying to get rid of us" -- sorry:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "I'm annoyed they're trying to get us in when trying to get rid of us."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: What was she talking about?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There were conversations around that time about not having band 4 nurses on the unit anymore --
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- so there was a discussion about whether those band 4s would lose their jobs.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's what she was referring to?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She is, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you appreciate what sort of day would be lying ahead of you before you went in for the shift on the 25th?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry, the 23rd. Let's have a look at the layout for that shift then, please, and we'll go to tile 106.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We'll remind ourselves: the shift leader, Melanie Taylor. You are the designated nurse there, Ms Letby, for [Baby O]. Also on duty, Samantha O'Brien, Christopher Booth, Yvonne Griffiths,
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yvonne Farmer, Rebecca Morgan. Do you remember who Rebecca Morgan was?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, a student nurse.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And Janet Cox. You'll find that at the front of the NNU if that helps -- NNU review. You should do.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we scroll down to see the actual layout, you tell us who you were looking after that day.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I was in nursery 2 with [Baby P] and [Baby O] and another baby, JD.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You were allocated all three?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And what level of care were these, the triplets, at this point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: High dependency.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What is the ratio meant to be for high dependency babies to nurses?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: One nurse to two babies.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So is this the correct --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The three babies here were high dependency.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that the correct ratio?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that outside the guidelines?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why is it necessary to have the right number of nurses for the right number of babies?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So that we can make sure we give each baby the care that they need.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is nursery 1, there's four babies in there. Is that the intensive care nursery?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What is the ratio of intensive care babies to nurses?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: One-to-one.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that being followed?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No. And the nursery is also full.
blocks.speaker: LETBY
